title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Asha Patel
summary: This consolidated company-wide policy document defines the standard processes and controls for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended to provide a single reference for employees and team leads to ensure consistent compliance with operational, security, and legal requirements.
toc: 8. Internal Templates & Where to Find Them
access_and_permissions:
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access to systems and data while enabling efficient onboarding and offboarding.

Scope: Applies to all employees, contractors, vendors, and service accounts that access Redwood Inference systems and data.

Standards and controls:
- Single Sign-On (SSO): All human users must authenticate via our corporate SSO (Okta). Service accounts must use short-lived keys or workload identity where supported.
- Role-based groups: Teams must use centralized IAM groups (e.g., eng-core-read, eng-core-write, infra-admin) managed in the Identity Directory. Do not grant permissions to individuals outside of groups unless approved.
- Approval workflow: Access requests are submitted via the Access Request form (People Ops portal). Required approvals: direct manager + owner_team (team admin). For sensitive systems (see list below) an additional Security approval is required.
- Sensitive systems: production data stores, KMS, vault, customer PII databases, and payroll systems. Requests for these systems require Security review and justification.
- Onboarding: People Ops triggers automated provisioning for standard role templates within 24 hours of new hire start date. Non-standard access must be requested separately.
- Offboarding: HR/People Ops must submit termination in HRIS. Automated deprovisioning runs within 1 hour for cloud/SaaS access; on-prem access revocation must be completed within 8 business hours.
- Access reviews: Quarterly access certification led by Security & People Ops. Team leads must review and attest to memberships. Remediation SLA: 7 days for removal of unused privileges.
- Temporary access: Timeboxed approvals (max 30 days by default). Extensions require manager + owner_team reapproval.
- Privileged access: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory. Privileged sessions are monitored and logged.

Owner: People Ops (operational), Security (policy & sensitive approvals).
change_management:
Purpose: Provide a predictable, auditable change process to reduce risk to production systems and ensure coordinated rollouts.

Scope: All changes touching production services, networking, IAM policies, core infra, and customer-facing APIs.

Change types and approval matrix:
- Standard changes (low-risk, repeatable): Pre-approved by CAB and do not require per-change approval; must use the standard change template in the change system. Typical examples: non-customer-impacting configuration refreshes. Window: weekdays 02:00-06:00 PT for infra-affecting scheduled runs.
- Normal changes: Require submission to the Change Advisory Board (CAB) with a 72-hour review cycle for major changes. Owners must include rollout plan, canary steps, monitoring checklist, and rollback plan.
- Emergency changes: Implemented outside normal windows only for incidents. Must be logged in the change system within 4 hours and post-facto reviewed by CAB within 48 hours.

Required artifacts for change submission:
1) Change request form (summary, owner, impacted services)
2) Risk assessment and impact matrix
3) Rollout plan including canary percentages and backout strategy
4) Monitoring/runbook links and SLOs to watch (latency > 150ms 95th for API routes triggers rollback)
5) Test sign-offs and stakeholder approvals (QA or service owner)

Rollout best practices:
- Canary deployments for code changes: 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% with minimum observation period (15m, 30m, 60m).
- Feature flags: Use feature flagging for gradual exposure.
- Automated rollbacks: CI/CD pipelines must support automated rollback on health-check failures.

Owner: eng-platform for platform services, eng-infra for infra changes, with CAB chaired by a rotating member of eng-sre.
data_management:
Purpose: Protect company and customer data through classification, lifecycle controls, encryption, and retention policies.

Data classification levels:
- Public: Intended for public distribution (e.g., marketing pages).
- Internal: Internal business data with no customer PII.
- Restricted: Customer or company sensitive data (customer identifiers, non-sensitive billing info).
- Confidential: Highly sensitive data (PII, payroll, secrets, encryption keys).

Handling rules by classification:
- Storage: Confidential and Restricted data must be stored in approved, encrypted repositories (encrypted at rest with KMS). Internal and Public may use standard collaboration tools with access controls.
- Transmission: Use TLS 1.2+ for all network traffic. Do not transmit PII via unapproved channels (e.g., personal email).
- Encryption: All production datasets are encrypted at rest with customer-specific KMS where required. KMS access is limited to security and infra service principals.
- Backups: Nightly backups for critical production databases. Backup retention: 90 days for operational backups, 7 years for billing/financial records as required by finance/legal.
- Retention & deletion: Data retention schedules are defined per dataset. Data deletion requests for personal data (DSARs) must be routed to Legal + Security and completed within 30 days where applicable.
- Data residency: When a customer requires region-specific residency, use the Private deployment options and follow the customer-specific deployment checklist in eng-private-deployments.
- Access control: Use least-privilege group membership; access to Restricted/Confidential systems requires documented business justification.
- Logging & monitoring: Access to sensitive datasets is logged centrally and reviewed during quarterly audits.

Owner: Security (policy) and Data Stewards (dataset owners).
procurement_and_expenses:
Purpose: Govern purchasing, contracting, and employee expense reimbursements to control spend and ensure legal/compliance review.

Procurement workflow and thresholds:
- Purchases < $5,000: Manager approval. Use the Purchase Request template and submit to Finance via Spend Management tool.
- Purchases $5,000- $50,000: Manager + Director approval; Procurement team review recommended.
- Purchases > $50,000: VP-level approval + Legal review for contract terms. Procurement team must be engaged early.
- SaaS and cloud vendors: All new SaaS/vendor purchases require a Security questionnaire and Legal review (see Vendor Management).
- Capital vs. expense: Finance will classify purchases; consult Finance for multi-year commitments.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit expense reports within 30 days. Original receipts or photos are required for all items > $25.
- Per diem: Domestic $75/day, international $200/day (covers meals & incidentals). Card use encouraged.
- Travel class: See Travel Policy (section 7).
- Lost receipts: Submit an affidavit form with manager sign-off; Finance reserves right to deny.

Corporate cards & limits:
- Corporate card issuance requires manager approval and Finance counter-signature. Monthly reconciliation by cardholder within 10 days of statement.

Owner: Finance (policy and approvals) with support from Procurement and People Ops.
vendor_management:
Purpose: Standardize vendor onboarding, risk assessment, contracting, and lifecycle review to mitigate third-party risk.

Onboarding checklist:
1) Vendor request form with business justification.
2) Security questionnaire (must pass minimum controls or compensate with contract terms). Requirements: SOC2 Type II report OR completed security questionnaire + remediation plan.
3) Legal contract review: Standard terms preferred; any deviations must be approved by Legal.
4) Procurement purchase order and budget confirmation.
5) Vendor classification: Low/Medium/High risk (based on data access, criticality, and access to PII).

Risk management and reviews:
- High-risk vendors (access to customer data/KMS/payroll) require annual security re-evaluation and quarterly meetings with the owner_team.
- Medium-risk vendors require biennial review.
- Monitoring: Contract KPIs, performance metrics, and SLAs tracked in the Vendor Registry.

Offboarding vendors:
- Revoke access within 24 hours of contract termination. Ensure return/destruction of data per contract terms and obtain certification when required.

Owner: Procurement (operational), Legal (contracting), Security (risk), and the requesting owner_team.
travel_policy:
Purpose: Provide safe, cost-effective, and compliant travel guidelines while supporting business needs.

Approvals and booking:
- All travel requires manager approval via the Travel Request template. International travel requires pre-approval from manager + Security for high-risk destinations.
- Preferred booking system: Concur (or company-designated travel vendor). Employees should use approved vendors for accommodations and flights to leverage corporate rates.

Class of travel and accommodations:
- Flights: Economy for flights < 6 hours. Premium economy permitted for 6-8 hours with manager approval. Business class allowed for flights > 8 hours with Director approval.
- Hotels: Book at business-class hotels; select hotels with corporate rates where possible. Single occupancy standard unless otherwise approved.
- Ground transport: Use ride-share or rental cars per safety guidelines. Car rentals require insurance check and approval for high-risk destinations.

Per diem and expenses:
- Per diem: Domestic $75/day; International $200/day. Receipts required for individual items outside per diem.
- Incidentals and emergency support: People Ops and Security provide emergency assistance and evacuation support where needed.

Health & safety:
- Employees traveling to high-risk jurisdictions must complete a pre-travel security briefing and register travel with Security.
- Vaccination and medical requirements: Follow local legal requirements and consult People Ops for required documentation.

Owner: People Ops (policy) with Security for high-risk travel reviews and Finance for expense reconciliation.

roles_and_responsibilities:
Owners and responsibilities (high level):
- People Ops: Onboarding/offboarding, employee-level access templates, travel approvals, and HR-related procurement.
- Security: Policy ownership for access, data classification, vendor security reviews, and quarterly audits.
- Finance: Procurement approvals, expense reimbursements, corporate card administration, and spend reporting.
- Procurement: Vendor onboarding operational execution, purchase orders, and vendor registry maintenance.
- Legal: Contract review and negotiation for vendors and large purchases.
- Eng-Platform / Eng-Infra: Change management implementation for platform and infra services.
- Team Leads/Managers: First-line approvers for access and expenses and periodic attestation for access reviews.

Escalation contacts: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.example.com), Security (security@redwood.example.com), Finance (finance@redwood.example.com).
compliance_and_audit:
Audit rhythm and evidence collection:
- Quarterly internal audits: Access certifications, change log sampling, and vendor controls evidence.
- Annual external audits: Support SOC2/ISO certification processes with requested evidence.
- Artifact retention: Maintain change request records, access review attestations, and vendor questionnaires for a minimum of 3 years unless legal requires longer.
- Continuous improvement: Post-audit remediation tickets are tracked in the compliance backlog with owners and SLA for remediation (typically 90 days for medium risk items).

Reporting violations and exceptions:
- Exceptions: Temporary exceptions to policy require documented justification, explicit approver (owner_team + Legal or Security as applicable), and defined expiration.
- Policy violations: Report via confidential incident reporting to Security and People Ops. Violations may result in disciplinary action per company handbook.

Owner: Security (audit coordination) and Compliance team.
